newsitem.title: POLAND: Cargill to build fifth feed plant in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Cargill to build fifth feed plant in Poland.

text.p: U.S. food trading and processing company Cargill Enterprises Inc. will start building its fifth animal feed plant in Poland later this year in Pruszcz near the northern city of Gdansk, a company official said on Tuesday.

"In August or September this year we expect to start building our fifth feed plant, in Pruszcz Gdanski...the construction will take about a year," Marcel Isler, director for feeds in Central and Eastern Europe, told a news conference.
He added that Cargill, which last year produced 190,000 tonnes of feed in Poland and has about five percent of the country's market, expects to double its production by the end of 1998.

Production is underway at feed plants in Sierpc and Siedlce and Isler said it would begin in summer this year at the company's third such factory at Krzemieniew near Leszno, in western Poland for which the site was bought in July 1996.

The firm's fourth plant at Ropczyce near Rzeszow in southeast Poland was acquired from a Polish firm in February and is now undergoing modernisation, with production due to begin in the third quarter of 1997.
Cargill produces feed mainly for pigs and poultry in Poland.
Last year Cargill said it wanted to invest $20-40 million by the year 2000 in the country, where it had already invested $58 million since 1992.
